### Short answer **`plaintext‑only` is *not* a boolean string** – it’s a special enumerated value that some browsers accept for the `contenteditable` attribute. If you need a true/false string, you should use `"true"` (because the element is still editable) or `"false"` (if you want to disable editing). --- ## What the spec says | Attribute | Standard values | Notes | |-----------|-----------------|-------| | `contenteditable` | `"true"`, `"false"`, `"inherit"` | These are the only values defined by the HTML 5 spec. | | `contenteditable` | `"plaintext-only"` | **Not part of the official spec**, but many browsers (Chrome, Edge, Safari) recognize it as a way to allow editing *without* formatting. | So, if you’re writing markup that must pass strict validation, you should avoid `"plaintext-only"` and stick to the three standard values. If you’re targeting modern browsers and want the “plain‑text‑only” behaviour, you can safely use `"plaintext-only"`. --- ## How to decide which string to output | Desired behaviour | Boolean string you can output | Recommended attribute value | |-------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------| | Element should be editable (any kind of editing) | `"true"` | `"true"` | | Element should be non‑editable | `"false"` | `"false"` | | Element should be editable but only plain text | `"true"` (or `"plaintext-only"` if you want the special behaviour) | `"plaintext-only"` | > **Tip:** If you’re using a helper function like `convertEnumeratedValue` that turns a key/value pair into a boolean string, you’ll want to add a special case for `"plaintext-only"` so it returns `"true"` (or simply passes the value through unchanged if you want to preserve the special behaviour). --- ## Practical example ```html
Edit me
Read‑only
Only plain text can be edited here
``` If you’re generating this markup programmatically: ```js function getContentEditableValue(isEditable, plainTextOnly) { if (plainTextOnly) return "plaintext-only"; return isEditable ? "true" : "false"; } ``` --- ### Bottom line - **Use `"plaintext-only"`** if you want the plain‑text‑only editing mode and you’re okay with browser‑specific behaviour. - **Use `"true"` / `"false"`** if you need strict compliance with the HTML spec or if you’re targeting environments where `"plaintext-only"` isn’t supported. That’s all you need to decide the correct string representation for the `contenteditable` attribute!
